None of the three retrieved precedents actually deal with the near-threshold structuring pattern seen in case_001 (12 feeder accounts sending 92.5-98.5%-of-CTR-threshold transfers into a single hub account within a 33-hour window, followed by rapid consolidated outbound layering). 

- case_013 involves a single transaction between two long-tenured, related accounts at an amount consistent with income — a benign one-off pattern, not a multi-feeder near-threshold structuring pattern. Not analogous.
- case_005 is a mule_hub fan-out (one account paying out to 20 counterparties) that was explained away as legitimate marketplace activity; it is a fan-out (one-to-many) rather than the fan-in (many-to-one near-CTR-threshold) pattern here, and the resolution hinged on marketplace/KYC corroboration that isn't present or analogous in this case.
- case_007 is a round-tripping (circular flow) typology, evaluated against an entirely different playbook (RT-1 through RT-3), not the structuring (STR-1 through STR-4) checklist matched here.

So while case_001 fully matches all four structuring playbook criteria (STR-1 through STR-4) — near-threshold inbound clustering, tight time window, rapid consolidated outbound layering, and one-off feeder relationships — I do not have a precedent in the retrieved set that shows how a genuinely analogous near-threshold structuring case was previously resolved (e.g., escalated, filed as SAR, or dismissed with a legitimate explanation). I'd recommend treating this as a novel/unprecedented pattern for decision purposes and escalating based on the strength of the STR-1–STR-4 match alone, rather than relying on the precedents above, since none of them address this typology or fact pattern directly. If you have a broader precedent set specifically tagged 'structuring,' it would be worth re-querying for those before finalizing a decision.
